items.headline: Fantasy football matchup rankings: Upgrade Tyler Warren, Tetairoa McMillan in Week 4
items.body:
Making tough lineup decisions each week can be the most challenging part of fantasy football. When you're torn between two similar players, start the player with the superior matchup.

But exactly how does one determine the best (and worst) weekly matchups?

The matchup rankings provide a schedule-independent method to evaluate positional matchups, ranking all 32 opposing defenses in order of most to least favorable for opposing players at all four skill positions. Instead of relying upon seasonal totals, we calibrate points-allowed data to show how each…

items.headline: Singleton didn't get a carry or a target in Sunday's Week 3 loss to the Giants.
items.body: Though head coach Robert Saleh suggested near the end of the week that Singleton could get more carries in Week 3, the rookie running back didn't end up seeing any action at all on offense. He did record 10 snaps on special teams, but that probably wasn't what fantasy managers had in mind. It appears that the rookie isn't yet in line for a significant role in the backfield as long as Tony Pollard and Tyjae Spears are both healthy.

items.headline: Ayomanor caught one of three targets for 11 yards in Sunday's Week 3 loss to the Giants.
items.body: Ayomanor didn't make much noise, but he finished with the second-most offensive snaps (48) among Tennessee's wideouts. while veteran Calvin Ridley dropped to 20 snaps and went without a catch for the second time in three weeks. Carnell Tate and Wan'Dale Robinson are the clear top WR options for Cam Ward, but Ayomanor may be claiming the No. 3 role. That said, Tennessee's air attack has been among the worst in the league, so none of the team's pass catchers make for a particularly appealing week-to-week fantasy asset.

items.headline: Fields caught both of his targets for 19 yards during the Giants' 12-7 win over the Titans on Sunday.
items.body: Fields' 44 snaps on offense were actually second-most among Giants wide receivers behind Malik Nabers (50), though the former finished fourth on the team in targets behind Nabers (six), tight end Isaiah Likely (five) and running back Cam Skattebo (four). Fields has logged two catches in each of the first three games of the regular season, but the rookie third-rounder and the rest of the Giants pass catchers will take on the Cardinals in Week 4, with Arizona's defense ranking second-to-last in fantasy points allowed to opposing wide receivers.

items.headline: Vele caught three of six targets for 39 yards Sunday in a loss to Las Vegas.
items.body: Tyler Shough had another big day at quarterback for the Saints, with 160 of his 255 passing yards going to the combination of No. 1 wideout Chris Olave and top tight end Juwan Johnson. Vele finished third behind that duo in both targets (six) and receiving yards (39). The third-year wideout has been locked into a key role in the Saints' passing game, and through three contests he's registered 15 catches on 22 targets for 172 yards and one touchdown.

items.headline: Harris turned nine carries into 52 yards during the Giants' 12-7 win over the Titans on Sunday.
items.body: Harris finished as a close second to Cam Skattebo (60) in rushing yards Sunday, but the former needed 11 less carries and averaged 5.8 yards per rush in the Giants' Week 3 win. Harris saw his usage on offense increase compared to Week 2 in what was his debut with the Giants, and it looks like he's settled in as the team's RB2 behind Skattebo and ahead of both Tyrone Tracy and Devin Singletary. Up next is a Week 4 road tilt against the Cardinals.

items.headline: Mendoza did not play in the Raiders' 35-27 Week 3 win over the Saints.
items.body: Kirk Cousins again took every snap under center for Las Vegas in the high-scoring victory. There was some thought before the start of the season that Mendoza could work his way into the starting role quickly if Cousins or the team struggled, but instead Las Vegas is 3-0 and the veteran QB is tied for the NFL lead with nine touchdown passes. Mendoza will continue to learn on the sidelines until Cousins slows down, but the first overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft is still expected to get his chance before the season is over.

items.headline: Bell caught four of seven targets for 67 yards in Sunday's 24-10 loss to Kansas City.
items.body: With Caleb Douglas (ankle) inactive and De'Von Achane suffering a torn ACL in the first half, Bell saw a biggest increase in playing time and opportunity. His seven targets were tied for second on the team with tight end Greg Dulcich, behind Malik Washington's 10. If Douglas needs to miss more time, Bell could again see elevated snaps Sunday against Minnesota.

items.headline: Wilson turned nine carries into 14 yards during the Seahawks' 33-31 loss to the Commanders on Sunday.
items.body: Wilson saw his role expand during a Week 2 win over the Cardinals after Jadarian Price left the game due to a chest injury, taking 21 carries for 92 yards. Wilson returned to a rotational role alongside George Holani in Week 3 after Price was cleared to play, but the former Packer still led the backfield with nine carries. Wilson has 32 carries for 109 yards (3.4 YPC) through the first three games of the season, and it looks like the Seahawks may be shifting to a committee approach with Price not yet seizing the lead role -- a committee that will get more crowded when Zach Charbonnet (knee) eventually comes off the PUP list.

items.headline: Washington caught five of 10 targets for 56 yards in Sunday's 24-10 loss to Kansas City. He gained five rushing yards on two carries.
items.body: Washington became the focal point of the Dolphins offense after De'Von Achane suffered a season-ending torn ACL in the first half. On the season, Washington has recorded 12 catches for 152 yards on a team-high 23 targets. He's also handed three rushing attempts for nine yards.

items.headline: Johnson carried the ball six times for 17 yards and returned one kickoff for 31 yards in Kansas City's 24-10 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.
items.body: Johnson played 13 offensive snaps and nine special-teams snaps in Sunday's contest. The rookie fifth-rounder continues to give Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker an occasional breather, but Johnson's role on offense doesn't figure to expand beyond that without an injury to the former Seahawk.

items.headline: Williams caught two passes on four targets for 15 yards during the Commanders' 33-31 win over the Seahawks on Sunday.
items.body: The rookie third-rounder's two catches both came in the second quarter. Williams' 28 offensive snap were third-most among Washington's wide receivers, ahead of Treylon Burks (25) and Dyami Brown (21) but well behind Terry McLaurin (52) and Stefon Diggs (41). Williams will take a 9-103-1 receiving line on 11 targets into a Week 4 clash against the Colts this Sunday in London, England.

items.headline: Cameron secured one of two targets for a 12-yard touchdown in Sunday's 35-6 win over the Patriots.
items.body: Cameron got the scoring started early in the second quarter, catching the first of Trevor Lawrence's three touchdown passes. The rookie ended up finishing with 23 offensive snaps against New England, the same amount as Brian Thomas but behind Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers, who both played 50 snaps on offense. Cameron could be pushing Thomas for the No. 3 receiver role in Jacksonville.

items.headline: Allen played 15 snaps exclusively on special teams during the Commanders' 33-31 win over the Seahawks on Sunday.
items.body: After being limited mostly to garbage time work through the first two weeks, the rookie sixth-rounder didn't see the field on offense against Seattle. Allen saw a heavy workload during the preseason, but he now faces additional competition for a spot on the gameday roster after Austin Ekeler was brought back Tuesday. The Commanders head to London for a Week 4 tilt against the Colts this Sunday.

items.headline: Okonkwo (hamstring) will travel with the Commanders to London ahead of the team's Week 4 game against the Colts this Sunday, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
items.body: A hamstring injury has prevented Okonkwo from playing in the last two games, leading to Ben Sinnott, John Bates and Colson Yankoff getting more snaps at tight end. Okonkwo signed a three-year contract with the Commanders in March following four years with the Titans, but if he's able to return Sunday he'll be working with a new QB in the short term in Marcus Mariota.

items.headline: TeSlaa caught all three of his targets for 66 yards in the Lions' 31-24 win over the Jets on Sunday.
items.body: Detroit's third receiver, TeSlaa played 48 percent of the offensive snaps against New York but made the most of his opportunities and ended up leading the team in receiving yards. With Jameson Williams continuing to struggle to get going early in the season, TeSlaa could start earning a couple more looks from Jared Goff. It's still unlikely to be enough to put TeSlaa in the redraft fantasy mix unless one of Williams or Amon-Ra St. Brown misses time with an injury.

items.headline: Jeudy finished Sunday's 21-18 victory against Carolina with no targets or touches.
items.body: It was the second straight week that Jeudy didn't log a reception, and this time he didn't even get a target (he logged just one in Week 2 versus Tampa Bay). The veteran wideout continues to be on the field fairly often -- he's recorded an offensive snap share of over 50 percent in each of the Browns' three contests, including Sunday when he played 51 percent. However, he doesn't seem to be clicking well with QB Deshaun Watson, and at this point fantasy managers have little reason to include him in their lineups.

items.headline: Coleman saw two targets and recorded a 37-yard catch during the Bills' 24-16 win over the Chargers on Sunday.
items.body: Coleman's practice reps during Week 3 prep were limited by an ankle injury, but he was cleared to play and ended up handling 32 of 66 offensive snaps (48.5 percent), third most among Bills wide receivers behind Khalil Shakir (48) and DJ Moore (42). Coleman was responsible for his team's longest play of the game late in the second quarter, setting up a one-yard TD for Josh Allen on the next play. Coleman is capable of making big plays, but it's hard to rely on him for consistent production when he's behind Moore, Shakir, tight end Dalton Kincaid and running back James Cook in the pecking order for targets. The Bills wrap up a three-game homestand this Sunday in an AFC East showdown against…

items.headline: Black turned four carries into 17 yards and failed to haul in his lone target during the 49ers' 36-30 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
items.body: Black accumulated 95 scrimmage yards on 22 touches through the first two games of the season while working behind Christian McCaffrey, but the rookie observed most of Sunday's game from the sidelines, seeing the field for only eight of the 49ers' 54 offensive snaps (14.8 percent). Keeping McCaffrey healthy is a top priority, but Black's workload is likely to remain erratic and dependent on game script. The 49ers will remain home in Week 4 to host the Broncos this Sunday.

items.headline: Bourne hauled in two passes on three targets for 22 yards during the Cardinals' 36-30 loss to the 49ers on Sunday.
items.body: Bourne's first target of the game came early in the first quarter, but he wasn't looked at by Jacoby Brissett again until late in the fourth, when the duo connected on passes of 14 and eight yards on back-to-back plays to set up a one-yard touchdown run by the QB. Bourne played 48 of 87 offensive snaps (55.2 percent), which was third-most among Cardinals wide receivers behind Michael Wilson (81) and Marvin Harrison (67). Bourne is up to a 12-108-0 receiving line on 14 targets through three regular-season games, ahead of Harrison in target volume but well behind Wilson and Trey McBride. Up next is a Week 4 road tilt against the Giants this Sunday.

items.headline: Dowdle (toe) was estimated as a non-participant on Tuesday's injury report, Nick Farabaugh of PennLive.com reports.
items.body: The Steelers held a walkthrough for the second time in as many days ahead of Thursday's contest against the Browns, and once again Dowdle was unable to get any work in. He was at least present Tuesday after not being spotted during the media-viewing portion of Monday's session, but he will presumably have to practice in some capacity Wednesday in order to have any chance of suiting up.

items.headline: Waddle is believed to be "fine" despite being seen wearing a walking boot on his right foot following Sunday's victory over the Rams, Sam Jane of The Denver Post reports.
items.body: The Broncos haven't indicated the specific nature of the issue, but it appears Waddle is not dealing with any sort of serious setback. The wideout's practice reps are likely to be limited early in the week, but so long as he sheds the boot quickly, he should be good to go for a Week 4 tilt against the 49ers.

items.headline: Wicks recorded two receptions for 32 yards on five targets in Monday's 27-7 loss to the Bears.
items.body: Though he didn't find paydirt, Wicks played a critical role on the Eagles' lone scoring drive late in the second quarter, leading off the possession with a 13-yard catch and run. He was otherwise held in check while the game was still competitive, with his other reception coming in the fourth quarter when the Bears had built a 20-point lead. Through his first three games with Philadelphia, Wicks has produced a 9-179-1 receiving line on 15 targets.

items.headline: Lemon recorded three receptions for 29 yards on four targets in Monday's 27-7 loss to the Bears.
items.body: After taking the field for north of 60 percent of the snaps in both of the Eagles' first two contests, Lemon wasn't a major beneficiary of the absence of tight end Dallas Goedert (knee). Even though the Eagles leaned more heavily on three-wide formations, Lemon saw only a slight uptick in playing time Monday, logging 35 of 50 snaps (70 percent). The rookie first-round pick appears to be little more than a tertiary option in the passing game at this stage of his career, as he's thus far been held to seven catches for 38 yards on nine targets through his first three NFL games.

items.headline: Bryant recorded two receptions for 44 yards and a touchdown on two targets in Sunday's 30-26 win over the Rams. He also scored on a two-point conversion.
items.body: Bryant reached the end zone for the first time this season with 7:44 left in the third quarter, connecting with quarterback Bo Nix on a five-yard catch. The second-year wideout has seen his snap share gradually climb through the first three weeks, topping out at 70 percent in Week 3. The Broncos have been without Marvin Mims (foot) for the past two games, however, so Bryant could see a slight downturn in playing time once the Denver receiving corps is at full strength.

items.headline: Freiermuth recorded two receptions for 30 yards on four targets and carried once for one yard in Sunday's 30-27 win over the Bengals.
items.body: Freiermuth took the field for 37 of the Steelers' 62 offensive snaps, with his 60 percent share placing him slightly behind fellow tight end Darnell Washington (47 snaps, 76 percent). The Steelers should continue to make ample use of two-tight-end sets to keep Freiermuth involved in their game plans, but since he doesn't project to see heavy target volume week to week, he'll remain a largely touchdown-dependent fantasy option.

items.headline: Dowdle (toe) was present for Tuesday's practice but was a non-participant, Nick Farabaugh of PennLive.com reports.
items.body: After sitting out Sunday's win over the Bengals due to a right toe injury, Dowdle will go down as a non-participant on the Steelers' first two Week 4 practice reports. Unless he's able to fit in some on-field work during Wednesday's session, he'll likely be ruled out ahead of Thursday's game in Cleveland. Dowdle's absence would set up Jaylen Warren for another heavy workload, after he handled 20 touches in Week 3.

items.headline: Ekeler signed a one-year contract with the Commanders on Tuesday, Zach Selby of the team's official site reports.
items.body: Ekeler will make his return to Washington for a third season, after his 2025 campaign came to an end after just two games due to a torn Achilles tendon. The 31-year-old received full medical clearance in the spring but remained unsigned through the first three weeks of the season before getting added to a Washington running-back room that includes Jacory Croskey-Merritt, Rachaad White and rookie Kaytron Allen. With White having established himself as the Commanders' top pass-catching/change-of-pace option out of the backfield, Ekeler may struggle to carve out a consistent role on offense.

items.headline: Knockout league pickups: Josh Allen, Justin Jefferson among big names available in Week 4
items.body:
If the 2026 NFL season is reiterating any key lesson, it's this: Anything goes.

The Las Vegas Raiders, 150-1 (0.66% implied odds) to win the Super Bowl at the onset of the season, are 3-0 with an 11.3-point average victory margin. Conversely, the Houston Texans, 18-1 (5.3%) entering Week 1, have dropped three in a row with their vaunted defense having surrendered the 14th-most points (25.0 per game).

…

items.headline: Fantasy football matchup rankings: Upgrade Ladd McConkey, Brock Purdy in Week 3
items.body:
Making tough lineup decisions each week can be the most challenging part of the fantasy football process. When you're torn between two similar players and simply don't know which one to start, start the player with the superior matchup.

Ah, but exactly how does one determine the best (and worst) weekly matchups?

The matchup rankings provide a schedule-independent method to evaluate positional matchups each week, ranking all 32 opposing defenses in order of most to least favorable for opposing players at the four skill positions (quarterback, running back, wide receiver and tight…

items.headline: Godwin gathered in three of four targets for 25 yards during Sunday's 23-16 loss to the Vikings.
items.body: Godwin ranked third among Buccaneers wide receivers in snap share (62 percent) behind Ted Hurst (75 percent) and Emeka Egbuka (74 percent) in Week 3, resulting in his least productive performance of the season. On top of that, Godwin hasn't been targeted more than four times in a game so far. With undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels set to be under center for at least a few contests as Baker Mayfield recovers from a dislocated right thumb, Godwin doesn't have an ideal situation in which to build momentum.

items.headline: The Giants released Beckham on Tuesday, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports.
items.body: Beckham's second stint in New York will end with a whimper, as he failed to haul in his lone target while playing just 20 total snaps over the Giants' first three games of the season. Since the 33-year-old wasn't able to earn consistent snaps in the receiver rotation and didn't contribute on special teams, the Giants deemed him an expandable piece. Beckham will look to find work elsewhere, but he could struggle to land with a team willing to give him meaningful playing time.

items.headline: Santos made both of his field-goal attempts and all three PATs in the Bears' 27-7 win over the Eagles on Monday night.
items.body: Santos made field goals from 29 yards and 48 yards in the contest. The kicker had a consistent night and now moves to 4-for-5 on field-goal attempts and a flawless 11-for-11 on PATs over three regular-season games in 2026.

items.headline: Shakir caught one of his three targets for six yards in the Bills' 24-16 win over the Chargers on Sunday.
items.body: Shakir played 71 percent of the Bills' offensive snaps in the contest but caught just one pass. The wide receiver was bullied in coverage while Josh Allen struggled on a day when the team's offense combined for five total turnovers.

items.headline: Bigsby caught his only target for five yards Monday in a Week 3 loss to the Bears. He also lost a fumble.
items.body: Bigsby logged 13 carries and scored a touchdown in Week 2 against Tennessee after Saquon Barkley suffered a stinger, but he went back to a minor role Monday. That was partly due to Barkley looking healthy and turning 15 totes into 82 yards, though Bigsby's lost fumble following his lone reception near the end of the first quarter also may have had a role in his lack of subsequent touches. Whatever the case may be, Bigsby doesn't seem likely to have a significant week-to-week role on offense whenever Barkley is healthy.

items.headline: Hockenson caught two of his four targets for 11 yards in the Vikings' 23-16 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.
items.body: Hockenson struggled along with the entire Vikings offense in the contest. The team relied on a single explosive rush and a single explosive pass play over the entire 60-minute game. Quarterback Kyler Murray was unable to stoke much of a passing attack against the Buccaneers, relying on a 41-yard touchdown to Jordan Addison for nearly a quarter of his passing yards on the night.

items.headline: Gadsden didn't catch any of his three targets in Sunday's loss to the Bills.
items.body: With Charlie Kolar (forearm) and David Njoku (fibula, IR) both unavailable, Gadsden drew the start Sunday and led Los Angeles' tight ends with a 57 percent offensive snap share. However, Gadsden couldn't do anything with that workload, failing to reel in any of the three targets QB Justin Herbert tossed his way. Gadsden could have another chance to make an impact this coming Sunday against Seattle with both Kolar and Njoku set to remain sidelined, but the Seahawks have given up the third-fewest receiving yards to tight ends so far this season.

items.headline: Monangai rushed 10 times for 31 yards and wasn't targeted in the Bears' 27-7 win over the Eagles on Monday night.
items.body: The second-year back logged exactly half of D'Andre Swift's workload on the ground, with Monangai handling his third straight 10-carry total to open the season. The Rutgers product saw his efficiency take a notable dip for the second consecutive game following a stellar Week 1 where he averaged 10.0 yards per carry, yet Monangai's role as a fairly high-volume No. 2 back in Chicago's offense is safe. The lack of receiving work Monday night was a disappointment after Monangai posted a 4-35-0 line through the air in the first two games, but he'll have a chance to atone in what should be a favorable Week 4 home matchup against the Jets on Sunday.

items.headline: Allgeier rushed twice for minus-1 yard and caught all four of his targets for 10 yards in the Cardinals' 36-30 loss to the 49ers on Sunday.
items.body: Rookie first-round pick Jeremiyah Love worked as the clear lead back for the first time in his nascent career Sunday, relegating Allgeier to a minor role. Allgeier was thus limited to screen passes and checkdowns, catching everything thrown his way for minimal gains. It remains to be seen if Sunday's notable shift in workload will have carryover into a Week 4 road matchup against the Giants on Sunday.

items.headline: Concepcion finished Sunday's 21-18 victory versus Carolina with two catches (on nine targets) for nine yards. He also returned one punt for one yard.
items.body: Concepcion actually tied tight end Harold Fannin for the team lead with nine targets, but the rookie wideout managed to haul in just two of those looks. His receptions went for five and four yards, continuing what has become a trend, as he's averaging a meager 6.7 yards per reception so far this season. The target share indicates that the Browns want Concepcion to be an integral part of the passing game, but so far he doesn't seem to be clicking with QB Deshaun Watson.

items.headline: Loveland secured all four targets for 31 yards in the Bears' 27-7 win over the Eagles on Monday night.
items.body: Head coach Ben Johnson appeared to make a concerted effort to get the ball into Loveland's hands Monday after the tight end's slow first two games, and that approach met with some success. While all three components of Loveland's receiving line qualified as season-high figures, the second-year pro's longest reception went for just 12 yards, and he was well behind the wideout trio of Kalif Raymond, Luther Burden and Rome Odunze in receiving yards. Loveland's chemistry with fill-in signal-caller Case Keenum was encouraging, however, and the duo should have a chance to continue working together in Sunday's Week 4 home matchup against the Jets.

items.headline: Odunze secured three of six targets for 44 yards in the Bears' 27-7 win over the Eagles on Monday night.
items.body: Odunze was relegated to a complementary role in the 20-point victory, finishing fourth in receptions and third in both receiving yards and targets for the Bears on a night in which Case Keenum filled in for Caleb Williams (hamstring) under center. While Odunze entered the season as the presumptive No. 1 receiver, veteran offseason addition Kalif Raymond, who had familiarity with head coach Ben Johnson's scheme from their mutual time with the Lions, has enjoyed an expanded role over the first three games while gathering in an impressive 19 of 21 targets. Conversely, Odunze is averaging a career-best 17.4 yards per reception but has a modest eight catches and no touchdowns through three…

items.headline: Burden secured seven of 11 targets for 61 yards and a touchdown while rushing once for seven yards in the Bears' 27-7 win over the Eagles on Monday night.
items.body: The second-year wideout led the Bears in receptions and targets in the impressive win with totals that also qualified as season highs, while checking in second only to Kalif Raymond in receiving yards. Burden also scored his first touchdown of the season on a nifty shovel pass that he took eight yards to the house while breaking multiple tackles near the goal line to cap off Chicago's opening possession. Burden's ability to click with fill-in signal-caller Case Keenum bodes well for the receiver's fantasy prospects, considering Caleb Williams (hamstring) is still projected to miss several more games. Burden will look to carry over the momentum into a Week 4 home matchup against the Jets on…

items.headline: Barner caught five of nine targets for 69 yards in the Seahawks' 33-31 loss to the Commanders on Sunday.
items.body: Barner saw an intense target share in Sunday's contest, picking up the slack for the Seahawks offense. The Commanders defense relentlessly prioritized Jaxon Smith-Njigba as the game developed, leaving Barner to see plenty of attention in a losing effort.

items.headline: Hurts completed 16 of 25 passes for 153 yards with no touchdowns and one interception while rushing four times for 25 yards and a touchdown in the Eagles' 27-7 loss to the Bears on Monday night.
items.body: Hurts scuffled through the air as much as his final line suggests, averaging a modest 6.1 yards per attempt while taking a pair of sacks. The star signal-caller also absorbed a big hit on the sideline at the end of a two-yard scramble midway through the second quarter, and he missed four plays while undergoing a concussion check he subsequently passed. Hurts led the Eagles to their only points upon checking back in for the following possession, one he capped off with a one-yard touchdown run as time expired in the first half. That would prove to be the highlight of an otherwise forgettable night, and Hurts is averaging an unremarkable 206.7 passing yards per game alongside a 5:3 TD:INT…

items.headline: Hurts exited Monday's game versus Chicago to be evaluated for a concussion and has since been cleared to return.
items.body: Hurts was pulled after taking a hard hit midway through the second quarter. He headed to the medical tent and was replaced at quarterback by Andy Dalton, who threw an interception in the end zone to end a potential Eagles scoring drive. Hurts now is slated to get back behind center for Philadelphia following the brief but costly exit.

items.headline: Marks turned five carries into 15 yards and a touchdown and hauled in his lone target for six yards during the Texans' 19-17 loss to the Colts on Sunday. He also returned two kickoffs for 52 yards.
items.body: Marks and David Montgomery both averaged only 3.0 yards per carry during Sunday's loss, though the former found the end zone for the first time this season on a one-yard rushing touchdown late in the fourth quarter. Marks' 20 snaps on offense was behind Montgomery's 34, though neither running back has found much success in the rushing attack in each of the Texans' last two games. Houston will look to avoid an 0-4 start to the season in Week 4 against Dallas.

items.headline: Tucker caught all four of his targets for 43 yards during Sunday's 35-27 win over New Orleans.
items.body: Tucker finished second on the team in targets, but he was far behind tight end Brock Bowers (13). The wide receiver was on the field for 40 of the team's 70 offensive snaps, and he was able to make it three straight games with at least two receptions to open the season. Tucker has now caught 11 of 15 targets for 189 yards and a touchdown to this point in 2026.

items.headline: Pittman caught two passes on five targets for 16 yards in Sunday's 30-27 win over the Bengals.
items.body: Pittman was cleared to return from a one-game absence due to a foot injury. Despite the low offensive output, he played 45 of 62 offensive snaps (72.3 percent), which was second-most among Steelers wide receivers behind DK Metcalf (56). Pittman also was tied for the second-most targets, though six Pittsburgh pass catchers were targeted at least four times by Aaron Rodgers. Pittman has a 5-74-0 receiving line (eight targets) across two regular-season contests heading into Thursday's game against the Browns, whose secondary could be without starters Grant Delpit (shoulder) and Tyson Campbell (knee).

items.headline: Likely caught two of five targets for 13 yards during the Giants' 12-7 win over the Titans on Sunday.
items.body: After logging 13 catches through the first two games of the regular season, Likely was held to only two receptions in Week 3, the first game with Jameis Winston as the starter instead of Jaxson Dart (knee, IR). Likely's five targets were second most on the Giants behind Malik Nabers (six), but the scoring floors of all Giants pass catchers figure to be lower with Winston under center. That said, New York could turn the keys over to the recently acquired J.J. McCarthy if Winston continues to underwhelm. The Giants will stay home for Week 4 against the Cardinals, whose defense gave up a 6-82-2 receiving line to tight end George Kittle in a 36-30 loss to the 49ers in Week 3.

items.headline: Andrews caught three of five targets for 24 yards during Sunday's 34-31 win over the Cowboys.
items.body: Andrews was limited by a hand injury that he suffered in the second quarter, and he was on the field for only 33 of the team's 64 offensive snaps. The tight end has recorded at least three catches in each of the team's first three games, reeling in 13 of 18 targets for 122 yards so far this season. Andrews has yet to reach the end zone this year, and his next chance will come against the Titans in Week 4.

items.headline: Davis played five snaps on offense and five snaps on special teams without showing up in the box score otherwise in the Bills' 24-16 win over the Chargers on Sunday.
items.body: Davis' catch for no gain early in the fourth quarter was negated by a holding penalty by Alec Anderson. It appears Davis will not be a factor in the Bills' offensive game plan this season, with Ty Johnson serving as the backup option in the backfield for James Cook. Davis should continue to see the field as a contributor on special teams, though he did not return a kickoff after doing so in both of the first two games of the regular season.

items.headline: Worthy caught both of his targets for 20 yards during Sunday's 24-10 win over the Dolphins.
items.body: Worthy entered Sunday's game on the heels of a 5-25-1 performance (on seven targets) during the Chiefs' Week 2 overtime win over the Colts. He didn't see any targets in the red zone Sunday compared to the three he had against Indianapolis, though he did lead all Chiefs wide receivers with 43 offensive snaps. His speed makes him a boom-or-bust candidate every week, though Worthy and the Chiefs pass catchers could thrive in a Week 4 road tilt against the Raiders if Las Vegas' rookie safety Treydan Stukes (concussion) is unable to play.

items.headline: Washington turned five carries into 54 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 35-27 win over the Saints.
items.body: Washington was only on the field for 11 of the team's 70 offensive snaps, but he still left his mark on the contest. Most notably, the running back broke loose for a 36-yard rushing touchdown late in the third quarter. Washington is a distant No. 2 option behind Ashton Jeanty in the Raiders backfield, but he now has rushed 15 times for 102 yards and a TD over three contests to open the 2026 campaign.

items.headline: Strange caught three of five targets for 32 yards during the Jaguars' 35-6 win over the Patriots on Sunday.
items.body: Most of Strange's production came on a 23-yard catch midway through the second quarter, which put the Jaguars just outside the red zone and helped lead to a 10-yard touchdown pass from Trevor Lawrence to Jakobi Meyers five plays later. Strange finished Sunday's game tied for the second-most targets and catches and third in receiving yards behind Meyers (64) and Parker Washington (40). Strange is off to a somewhat slow start to the 2026 season, though he's competing against Meyers, Washington and Brian Thomas for targets in the passing game. Strange will take a 7-72-1 line (on 10 targets) into a Week 4 road clash against the Bengals.

items.headline: Boston caught two of four targets for 41 yards during the Browns' 21-18 win over the Panthers on Sunday. He also caught a two-point conversion.
items.body: The rookie second-rounder was held without a catch until the fourth quarter, when he caught 28- and 13-yard passes from Deshaun Watson before the duo connected on a two-point conversion late in the fourth quarter to extend the Browns' lead to three points. Boston was unable to record a touchdown catch for a third-straight game, though he still finished Sunday's contest as the Browns' second-leading receiver behind tight end Harold Fannin (51). Boston, Fannin and rookie first-rounder KC Concepcion will continue to serve as Watson's top targets in the passing game, with Jerry Jeudy and Isaiah Bond working in rotation. Boston will take a 9-195-2 receiving line (on 15 targets) into Thursday's…

items.headline: Ferguson caught three of five targets for 23 yards and a touchdown while also losing a fumble during Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Ravens.
items.body: Ferguson was able to reach the end zone for the second straight week, connecting with quarterback Dak Prescott for a 19-yard score in the third quarter. The tight end did have a mishap early in the fourth quarter, losing a fumble after reeling in a short pass from Prescott. Ferguson now has hauled in nine of 11 targets for 72 yards and three touchdowns over three contests this season, and he'll face a tough test against the Texans' dominant defense in Week 4.

items.headline: Doubs hauled in three of four targets for 49 yards during the Patriots' 35-6 loss to the Jaguars on Sunday.
items.body: Doubs finished second on the Patriots in both catches and receiving yards to Mack Hollins, the latter of whom finished with a 6-87-0 line on nine targets. Doubs and Hollins will continue to operate as Drake Maye's top targets in the absence of A.J. Brown (ankle), who will miss at least the next two weeks while on injured reserve. Doubs will take a 6-145-0 line on 11 targets into a Week 4 road matchup against Buffalo.

items.headline: Diggs caught four of seven targets for 33 yards during Sunday's 33-31 win over the Seahawks.
items.body: Diggs finished second on the team in targets behind fellow wideout Terry McLaurin, but he was unable to make it three straight games with a touchdown. Diggs has now recorded at least four receptions in each of his first three contests as a member of the Commanders, reeling in 13 of 22 targets for 135 yards and three scores. Backup quarterback Marcus Mariota proved to be a viable starter in Week 3 with Jayden Daniels (elbow) unavailable, so fantasy managers don't have to worry about Diggs moving forward.

items.headline: Johnston caught three of six targets for 40 yards during Sunday's 24-16 loss to the Bills.
items.body: Johnston finished second on the team in targets, and his 40 receiving yards were nearly double his previous season total of 24 yards. He and the rest of the Chargers offense have yet to find their stride in 2026, making him hard to trust as a fantasy asset. The wide receiver will look to get back on track in a tough matchup in Week 4 against the Seahawks.

items.headline: Rodriguez turned eight carries into 37 yards and a touchdown during the Jaguars' 35-6 win over the Patriots on Sunday.
items.body: Rodriguez made his way to the end zone for the first time this season on a five-yard rushing touchdown late in the third quarter to extend the Jaguars' lead to 28-3. The 2023 sixth-rounder played only 13 of 62 offensive snaps (21.0 percent), well behind Bhayshul Tuten (30) and just ahead of LeQuint Allen (eight). Rodriguez has 20 carries for 73 yards (3.7 YPC) and a score through three regular-season games, and he'll continue to operate as the backup option out of the backfield behind Tuten. The Jaguars hit the road for a Week 4 tilt against the Bengals.

items.headline: Gainwell turned three carries into minus-4 yards and added two catches (on five targets) for 14 yards in Sunday's 23-16 loss to the Vikings. He also returned six kickoffs for 160 yards and added a tackle.
items.body: Gainwell now is averaging just 2.1 yards per carry through the first three games of the regular season. He was utilized heavily as a pass catcher with the Steelers in 2025, but so far he has only six receptions (on 10 targets) for 22 yards. His 32 snaps on offense was slightly fewer than Bucky Irving (36), but the scoring floor of Gainwell and the rest of the Buccaneers' skill players will likely be lower for at least the next three weeks without Baker Mayfield (thumb) at the helm. Undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels will be the Bucs' QB1 in Mayfield's absence, starting with a Week 4 home tilt against the Packers this Sunday.

items.headline: Coach Sean McVay said Monday that Ferguson "likely" will be sidelined for Sunday's game in Philadelphia, Adam Grosbard of The Orange County Register reports.
items.body: Ferguson missed a portion of Sunday's loss at Denver to get X-rays on an ankle injury, and while he was cleared to return, he finished fourth among Rams tight ends in offensive snaps (22 of 86) behind Tyler Higbee (61), Colby Parkinson (37) and Davis Allen (31). Through three games this season, Ferguson had a 6-54-1 line on nine targets in Week 2 versus the Giants and one catch (on three targets) for nine yards in the other two contests. Now that he's slated to miss some time, the aforementioned trio likely will handle the bulk of the TE workload for L.A., though rookie Max Klare might finally see his first offensive plays.

items.headline: Head coach Sean McVay said Monday that the Rams are "hopeful" Nacua (hip) will return to action for Sunday's game at Philadelphia, Adam Grosbard of The Orange County Register reports.
items.body: Nacua has missed the past two gams due to a hip injury (on official practice reports) or what McVay alternatively has called "soreness in his groin" that's unrelated to the psoas discomfort the wide receiver dealt with in training camp. McVay relayed to Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com on Friday that if Nacua doesn't play Sunday at Denver, which came to pass, he likely will be available Week 4. McVay was more subdued Monday, also telling Gary Klein of the Los Angeles Times that Nacua's upcoming status is "to be determined." As a result, the will he or won't he suit up with Nacua likely will continue until close to next weekend's kickoff or even beyond that point.

items.headline: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said that Okonkwo (hamstring) will make the trip to London and will practice in some capacity leading up to Sunday's game against the Colts, Nicki Jhabvala of The Athletic reports.
items.body: Okonkwo has been sidelined for the Commanders' last two games due to the hamstring injury, which he sustained during the season-opening loss to the Eagles. He wasn't able to practice at any point in the last two weeks, but the tight end looks poised to take a step forward in that regard in Week 4. Okonkwo will presumably need to upgrade to full participation by Friday in order for the Commanders to clear him to play against the Colts.

items.headline: Bills head coach Joe Brady downplayed any concern about Allen's health after the quarterback took a hit to his knee area during the fourth quarter of Sunday's 24-16 win over the Chargers, Alex Brasky of SI.com and Alec…
items.body: With just under 10 minutes remaining in the fourth quarter, a Chargers defender appeared to plow into the side of Allen's left knee at the end of an eight-yard run, leaving the quarterback grimacing in pain afterward. Allen didn't end up missing any snaps and even handled a designed run later on during that same possession, but he was seen favoring the knee in the locker room after the game, per Chris Trapasso of BuffaloRumblings.com. Allen could receive some extra treatment over the next several days while he continues to manage the knee issue, but Brady offered no indication that the star quarterback is at any risk of sitting out next Sunday's game against the Patriots.

items.headline: Allen and Isaiah Davis will man the Jets backfield for as long as Breece Hall (thigh) is potentially sidelined, Rich Cimini of ESPN.com reports.
items.body: Hall exited in the fourth quarter of Sunday's loss at Detroit due to a thigh injury, and afterward he relayed that he "felt something" while running, per Brian Costello of the New York Post. Ian Rapoport and Adam Schefter of ESPN then reported Monday that Hall is considered week-to-week. While Hall hasn't outright been ruled out for Week 4 or beyond, Allen currently ranks second on the team in carries with 19, which have gone for 61 yards, while Davis hasn't logged an offensive snap through three contests to begin the season. As a result, Allen is the better bet to take advantage of an absent Hall, if that comes to pass.

items.headline: The Dolphins placed Achane (knee) on injured reserve Monday.
items.body: Achane's move to injured reserve was merely a formality after head coach Jeff Hafley confirmed earlier Monday that the running back would be lost for the season after sustaining an ACL tear in his left knee during Sunday's 24-10 loss to Kansas City. With Achane out of the mix for the rest of 2026, the Dolphins are left with Jaylen Wright (foot) and Ollie Gordon as the lone running backs on the 53-man roster.

items.headline: Head coach John Harbaugh reaffirmed that Winston is the Giants' starting quarterback after the team acquired J.J. McCarthy from the Vikings on Monday, Evan Barnes of Newsday reports.
items.body: While stepping in for the injured Jaxson Dart (knee) in Week 3, Winston threw for just 118 yards on 22 pass attempts in adverse weather conditions during the Giants' 12-7 win over the Titans. Despite his pedestrian numbers, Winston played turnover-free football, and that performance looks as though it will give him some job security even after the Giants added McCarthy, a 2024 first-round draft pick, to their quarterback room. Even though Dart is likely out for the season, Winston will still likely need to limit mistakes and keep the Giants competitive in his future starts in order to ward off McCarthy from supplanting him on the depth chart. Next up for Winston and the Giants is a home…

items.headline: Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley said Douglas (ankle) is day-to-day and could practice Wednesday, Travis Wingfield of the team's official site reports.
items.body: Douglas was inactive for Sunday's 24-10 loss to the Chiefs due to the ankle injury, but the Dolphins are seemingly optimistic that his absence won't extend beyond that. The rookie wideout has carved out a notable role right off the bat for Miami, logging snap shares north of 85 percent in both of the team's first two games while producing a 7-113-0 line on 10 targets.

items.headline: Hall is considered week-to-week after an MRI on Monday revealed that his thigh injury isn't significant as feared, Ian Rapoport and Adam Schefter of ESPN report.
items.body: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn shed more light on the severity of Hall's injury when he speaks to the media Wednesday, but the running back seemingly avoided any sort of major damage to his thigh that would result in an extended stint on injured reserve. However, with Hall being classified as week-to-week, he may be facing an uphill battle to make it back for the Jets' next game Sunday at Chicago. After Hall exited in the fourth quarter of this past Sunday's 31-24 loss to the Lions, Braelon Allen handled six touches over the Jets' final two possessions. Allen and Isaiah Davis would both be in store for expanded roles if Hall ends up missing any time.

items.headline: Head coach Jeff Hafley said Monday that he considers Wright (stinger/foot) to be "day-to-day," Joe Schad of The Palm Beach Post reports.
items.body: Wright's health is notable considering the Dolphins lost No. 1 RB De'Von Achane to a torn ACL during Sunday's loss to the Chiefs. Having said that, Hafley also called Wright "day-to-day" last Monday after he emerged from Week 2 at San Francisco with a stinger and foot injury, which didn't allow him to play Week 3. Wright likely will need to get through this week without a DNP to put himself in the running to help cover for the absent Achane. Currently, Ollie Gordon is the only healthy running back on Miami's active roster.

items.headline: Saints head coach Kellen Moore said that Etienne will have some "time lost" due to the hamstring injury he sustained in Sunday's 35-27 loss to the Raiders, Mike Triplett of NewOrleans.Football reports.
items.body: Moore noted that a specific timeline for Etienne's return hasn't been established, making it uncertain whether or not the running back will be able to avoid a stint on injured reserve. At the very least, Etienne will be sidelined for the Saints' Week 4 game against the Falcons next Monday, which likely paves the way for Alvin Kamara to take on an expanded profile in the backfield after working in a complementary role the previous two weeks. Reserve backs Kendre Miller and CJ Donaldson also should be in store for more opportunities for however long Etienne is out.

items.headline: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said Monday that he still has no update regarding how long Reed (neck) will be sidelined, Matt Schneidman of The Athletic reports.
items.body: Reed is just over a week removed from sustaining a serious-looking neck injury during the Packers' Sept. 20 win over the Jets, which resulted in the wide receiver being stretchered off the field and required an overnight hospital stay. Since Reed returned to Green Bay, the Packers haven't provided many details on his status, as the 26-year-old is seemingly still being evaluated before a timeline for a return is established. Though LaFleur didn't definitively rule Reed out for a Week 4 matchup against the Buccaneers, all signs point to the wideout missing a second straight game.

items.headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen reiterated Monday that Pierce didn't undergo surgery on his left heel and is continuing to rehab the injury, James Boyd of The Athletic reports.
items.body: Ian Rapoport of NFL Network had previously relayed last week that Pierce would avoid another procedure after aggravating his surgically repaired heel in a Sept. 20 loss to the Chiefs, but that report was called into question after the wideout was spotted Sunday moving around the Colts locker room with the aid of a scooter while he had a cast on his left foot. Apparently, Pierce is using the cast for extra protection and using the scooter to keep weight off the injured foot, which he hopes will accelerate the healing process. Pierce is without a timeline to return to game action, but he'll have to miss at least three more contests after landing on injured reserve over the weekend.

items.headline: Head coach DeMeco Ryans said Monday that he's "hopeful" to have Collins available for the Texans' Week 4 game against the Cowboys, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
items.body: Collins is working his way back from a Grade 1 hamstring strain, which has kept him from playing in either of the Texans' last two games. He hasn't practiced during the past two weeks either, so Collins would likely need to get back on the field as at least a limited participant at some point between Wednesday and Friday to have a realistic chance at suiting up against the Cowboys on Sunday. The Texans' playoff hopes have already taken a hit following an 0-3 start to the season, but the potential return of their No. 1 receiver could invigorate an offense that has struggled in his absence over the past two weeks.

items.headline: Head coach Todd Bowles said that Irving won't be included on the Buccaneers' Week 4 injury report, despite missing the final two possessions of Sunday's 23-16 loss to the Vikings, Scott Smith of the team's official…
items.body: Bowles didn't specify why Irving was off the field late in Sunday's contest, but any physical issue the running back might have been dealing with doesn't look like it will prevent him from playing Week 4. Despite logging a season-low 51 percent snap share, Irving still earned 17 touches (15 carries, two receptions) and accounted for 58 yards from scrimmage. He remains locked in as the clear No. 1 option out of the backfield over free-agent pickup Kenny Gainwell, who is averaging just 2.1 yards per carry and 3.7 yards per reception through three games.

items.headline: Brown was spotted Monday in the Patriots' locker room walking without a limp and wearing a small wrap on his injured right ankle, Taylor Kyles of CLNSMedia.com reports.
items.body: Kyles noted that Brown was wearing cleats, which could hint that he was able to do some on-field exercises. After being placed on injured reserve Sept. 12, Brown won't be eligible to start practicing with his teammates until Week 6, but the wideout at least seems to be making good progress in his recovery from the high-ankle sprain he sustained in the season-opening loss to the Seahawks.

items.headline: Head coach Todd Bowles said Monday that Daniels will step in as the Buccaneers' new starting quarterback while Baker Mayfield is out for a "minimum of three weeks" due to a dislocated right thumb, Cameron Wolfe of NFL…
items.body: The undrafted rookie made his NFL debut in relief of an injured Mayfield late in Sunday's 23-16 loss to the Vikings, rushing once for nine yards while failing to complete his first two pass attempts of the day before being intercepted on a Hail Mary as time expired. Since an MRI ruled out any damage to his thumb beyond the dislocation, Mayfield is expected to avoid a stint on injured reserve, but he doesn't appear in line to return to the lineup any sooner than Week 8 at Carolina. As a result, Daniels is now set to get his first extended NFL action beginning this Sunday, when the Buccaneers will host the Packers. During his six-year college career at Kansas, Daniels displayed some decent…

items.headline: Fantasy football free agent pickups: Gordon leads options to replace Achane for Week 4 and beyond
items.body:
Each Monday, before the current NFL week ends, we will identify players worthy of your attention who are available in at least 50% of ESPN standard leagues. Things change quickly for player valuation and roles each week in the NFL, and free agency is a critical way to acquire players. We are here to help!

Top pickup options at every position

Looking for the top recommendation at each skill position? Look no further! Here are the players to target heading into Week 3, along with their current roster percentages and a recommendation of how much of your free agent budget (FAB)…

items.headline: Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles said Monday that Mayfield (thumb) is expected to miss three weeks, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
items.body: Earlier Monday, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reported than an MRI on Mayfield's dislocated right thumb ruled out a fracture as well as any tendon or ligament damage. While Mayfield appears set to avoid surgery, he'll still need some time off to regain strength in his thumb so that he can properly grip the football and throw accurately and at full velocity. Per Cameron Wolfe of NFL Network, Bowles said that Mayfield won't be placed on injured reserve, so the Buccaneers could be targeting their Week 10 game in Carolina for his return to the lineup. Undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels will step in as the Buccaneers' new starting quarterback beginning with Sunday's game versus Green Bay.

items.headline: Mayfield underwent an MRI on his dislocated right thumb Monday that revealed no fracture, tendon or ligament damage, but the quarterback is still expected to miss time, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.
items.body: Mayfield is scheduled to get a second opinion on his thumb, so the Buccaneers may not provide a formal timeline for his recovery until he meets with another specialist. That being said, the dislocated thumb on his throwing hand will inhibit Mayfield's ability to grip the football, so the Buccaneers are expected to hold him out for at least their Week 4 game. Undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels came on in relief of Mayfield late in Sunday's 23-16 loss to the Vikings and looks on track to make his first NFL start this weekend at home against the Packers.

items.headline: Coker has been diagnosed with a minor quadriceps strain and could be available to play in next Sunday's game against the Lions, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
items.body: Coker made an early exit from Sunday's 21-18 loss to the Browns due to the quad issue, but follow-up tests Monday appear to have revealed nothing overly significant. That being said, Coker's status for Week 4 is still up in the air, with his practice activity Wednesday through Friday likely to be the determining factor in whether he plays. Despite leaving early in Week 3 in addition to being a regular on injury reports ahead of the Panthers' last two games due to an ankle issue, Coker has gotten off to a stellar start to the season with an 18-222-2 receiving line on 22 targets.

items.headline: Week 3 winners and losers: Gibbs and JSN stay hot; St. Brown and Taylor go quiet
items.body: Week 3 of the 2026 fantasy football season featured huge games by Seahawks WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Lions RB Jahmyr Gibbs. On the flip side, fantasy stars Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jonathan Taylor and

items.headline: Achane (knee) was diagnosed Monday with a torn ACL and will miss the remainder of the season, Ian Rapoport and Adam Schefter of ESPN report.
items.body: After Achane was forced out early in Sunday's 24-10 loss to the Chiefs, Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley acknowledged that he wasn't optimistic about the initial evaluations of the running back's injury. Follow-up testing Monday confirmed the Dolphins' worst fears, as the team's top playmaker will now be headed for season-ending surgery. Assuming he experiences no setbacks during what will be a lengthy rehab process, Achane could be ready to go for Week 1 of the 2027 campaign, but the Dolphins will now be left with Jaylen Wright (foot/stinger) and Ollie Gordon as their main backfield options for the final 14 games of 2026.

items.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said that he won't have an update on Hall's (thigh) status until Wednesday, Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic reports.
items.body: Hall departed Sunday's 31-24 loss to the Lions in the fourth quarter due to a thigh injury, finishing the contest with 13 carries for 32 yards and three catches for 23 yards. The running back will presumably undergo imaging Monday or Tuesday as the Jets look to determine the severity of his injury, and it's possible that the results of his medical tests could be reported before Glenn addresses the media Wednesday, when the team holds its first practice of Week 4. Until more details about his injury are known, Hall should be viewed as questionable for next Sunday's game in Chicago, with Braelon Allen being the next man up in the backfield if Hall can't play.

items.headline: Ekeler is expected to sign with the Commanders, pending a physical, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
items.body: Ekeler's 2025 campaign was cut short by a torn Achilles sustained a little over a year ago, but he was cleared to participate in football activities in April. As long as he checks out fine during his physical, Ekeler looks as though he'll be signed to the 53-man roster. The 31-year-old spent the previous two seasons in Washington and will likely handle a complementary role out of the backfield.

items.headline: Higbee caught eight of 11 targets for 62 yards and a touchdown during Sunday night's 30-26 loss to the Broncos.
items.body: Higbee went from having no targets in Week 2 to leading the team with eight catches while finishing second only to wide receiver Davante Adams (13) in targets one week later. The tight end reeled in his first touchdown of the year to cap off the team's second possession of the game, connecting with quarterback Matthew Stafford for a five-yard score. Higbee may have seen the added opportunities as a result of fellow tight end Terrance Ferguson sustaining an ankle injury in the first quarter, but Ferguson was able to return to action. Higbee will have a chance to prove that his performance wasn't an anomaly when the team hosts Philadelphia in Week 4.

items.headline: Sutton caught three of seven targets for 46 yards in Sunday's 30-26 win over the Rams.
items.body: Sutton led the team in receiving yards Sunday night while tying for the team lead in targets with RJ Harvey and Jaylen Waddle. This was a step in the right direction after Sutton mustered just 36 receiving yards over the previous two games combined. Between the offseason acquisition of Waddle and the change in play callers from Sean Payton to Davis Webb, Sutton has taken a step back early in the 2026 season after exceeding 1,000 receiving yards in each of the previous two regular seasons and catching 15 touchdown passes over that span. Sutton is still searching for his first TD of the campaign heading into a Week 4 road game against the 49ers.

items.headline: Dobbins rushed 17 times for 49 yards while catching one of two targets for four yards in Sunday's 30-26 win over the Rams.
items.body: Dobbins is up to 35 rushing attempts through three weeks, while no other Denver running back has exceeded 10. Jonah Coleman (ankle) was placed on injured reserve Saturday, while RJ Harvey has more targets (11) than carries (five). Dobbins has yet to score on the ground after recording four rushing touchdowns last season, and he has been a non-factor in the passing game, as Sunday's targets were Dobbins' first two of the season. On the bright side, Dobbins has recovered from previous hip and hamstring concerns and is poised to keep leading Denver's ground game in Week 4 at San Francisco.

items.headline: Harvey (hamstring) rushed twice for six yards while catching six of seven targets for 41 yards in Sunday's 30-26 win over the Rams.
items.body: Harvey didn't see much involvement on the ground but tied for the team lead in targets in his return from a one-game absence due to a hamstring injury. He was evaluated for a concussion in the second half and cleared to return, though Harvey had just one touch after that point. J.K. Dobbins is likely to keep working as Denver's primary rushing option in Week 4 against the 49ers, especially with rookie fourth-round pick Jonah Coleman (ankle) on IR, while Harvey remains the preferred running back in passing situations.

items.headline: Little hit all five of his extra-point attempts and missed a 70-yard field-goal try in Sunday's 35-6 win over the Patriots.
items.body: The Jaguars lined up for what would have been a record-setting field goal just before halftime, but Little missed it wide right. The kicker has failed to connect on only two attempts this season, a 54-yard field-goal try and this 70-yard attempt. The Jaguars have been offering him plenty of scoring opportunities through three games, and it's clear that the team doesn't hesitate to test Little's strong leg.

items.headline: Corum rushed six times for 15 yards and caught two of four targets for no gain during Sunday night's 30-26 loss to Denver.
items.body: Corum saw nine less carries than backfield mate Kyren Williams in Week 3, the widest discrepancy between the two in a contest so far this season. Corum did get his highest amount of targets in a contest since he logged four targets against the Colts in Week 4 of the 2025 campaign, though he didn't really do much with his two catches Sunday. The running back has now rushed 28 times for 148 yards while catching three of five targets for 13 yards over three games to open the 2026 season.

items.headline: Nix completed 17 of 34 passes for 186 yards, two touchdowns and one interception in Sunday's 30-26 win over the Rams. He also rushed four times for seven yards and a touchdown in addition to throwing two successful…
items.body: Nix threw for just 53 yards in the first half as the Broncos took a 16-0 deficit into the locker room. Denver turned things around in the third quarter, tying things up at 16-16 heading into the fourth quarter thanks to touchdown passes of five yards to Pat Bryant and eight yards to Nate Adkins, which were followed up by two-point conversions for Jaylen Waddle and Bryant, respectively, all thrown by Nix. The dual-threat QB made his biggest play down the stretch on the ground, powering in the go-ahead one-yard touchdown with 47 seconds left in the fourth quarter after being ruled out just short of the goal line on the preceding play. Denver's defense picked off Matthew Stafford on the…

items.headline: Waddle caught two of seven targets for 10 yards in Sunday's 30-26 win over the Rams. He also rushed once for 14 yards and caught a two-point conversion.
items.body: The highlight of Waddle's night came on the two-point conversion after Denver's first touchdown in the third quarter. Bo Nix dropped a pass just over a defender's helmet and Waddle came down with it while getting both feet down in the corner of the end zone to cut Denver's deficit to 16-8. Waddle tied for the team lead with seven targets, matching the totals of Courtland Sutton and RJ Harvey, who were two of the five players that topped Waddle's total in receiving yards Sunday night. The prized offseason acquisition is off to an inconsistent start with the Broncos ahead of a Week 4 trip to San Francisco, sandwiching a 138-yard outburst in Week 2 between two games in which he recorded a…

items.headline: Fairbairn connected on a 24-yard field goal and both of his extra-point tries in Sunday's 19-17 loss to the Colts.
items.body: The kicker made the most of his opportunities Sunday. He just didn't have very many, which has been a theme this season, as the Texans have given him just six PATs through three contests.

items.headline: Adams caught seven of 13 targets for 137 yards in Sunday's 30-26 loss to the Broncos.
items.body: Adams continued to thrive as Matthew Stafford's top target in the absence of Puka Nacua (hip). During Nacua's two-game absence, Adams has compiled 15 catches for a whopping 332 yards and two touchdowns. Adams led the NFL with 14 touchdown receptions during the 2025 regular season and is showing no signs of slowing down at age 33 early in the 2026 campaign. He is poised to maintain a prominent role in Week 4 against the Eagles, though the Rams are optimistic that Nacua could be cleared to return by then.

items.headline: Bates made a 30-yard field goal and all four of his extra-point tries in Sunday's 31-24 win over the Jets.
items.body: The third-year pro is now 12-for-12 on extra-point attempts and 3-for-3 on field-goal tries in 2026. Bates is also the beneficiary of an offense that has scored 31 points in all three games so far.

items.headline: Williams rushed 15 times for 88 yards while catching six of seven targets for 70 yards in Sunday's 30-26 loss to the Broncos.
items.body: Williams was far more effective than Blake Corum, who turned six carries and four targets into just 15 scrimmage yards. Williams' season-opening touchdown streak came to a halt at two games, but he has been one of the league's top all-around performers at running back in the early going, averaging 5.6 yards per carry while catching 11 of 12 targets and scoring a touchdown apiece as a rusher and a receiver. The Rams are off to a 1-2 start heading into a Week 4 trip to Philadelphia, so expect Los Angeles to continue leaning heavily on its top backfield option in an effort to avoid losing more ground in the NFC standings.

items.headline: Downs caught five of 11 targets for 77 yards during Sunday's 19-17 win over Houston.
items.body: Downs garnered the most targets on the team, narrowly edging out tight end Tyler Warren (10), while his 77 receiving yards led the way for Indianapolis. With Alec Pierce (heel) sidelined for the foreseeable future, Downs appears to have taken command as the team's No. 1 option at wide receiver. Over three games to open the regular season, the wideout has reeled in 14 of 24 targets for 186 yards, and he'll look to secure his first touchdown of the season in Week 4 against the Commanders.

items.headline: Stafford completed 30 of 55 passes for 390 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions in Sunday's 30-26 loss to the Broncos. He also rushed twice for 13 yards.
items.body: Stafford guided the Rams to a 16-0 halftime lead courtesy of a five-yard touchdown pass to Tyler Higbee followed by three Harrison Mevis field goals. LA's lead was erased in the third quarter, and after retaking the lead in the fourth, Stafford threw a disastrous pick-six that Talanoa Hufanga took 66 yards to the house to give the Broncos their first lead with 4:49 remaining. That pick-six was the 33rd Stafford has thrown in his regular-season career, surpassing Brett Favre for sole possession of first place in that dubious stat. Stafford was unfazed by that mistake and responded with a four-play, 77-yard touchdown drive, capped by a 48-yard touchdown pass to Konata Mumpfield, but Hufanga…

items.headline: Hurst caught one of three targets for a 40-yard touchdown during Sunday's 23-16 loss to Minnesota.
items.body: Hurst made the most of his one catch, notching his first career touchdown on a 40-yard deep ball from quarterback Baker Mayfield in the first quarter. The wide receiver has now caught six of 13 targets for 103 yards and a touchdown over the Bucs' first three regular-season games. Mayfield suffered a thumb injury in the fourth quarter and seems likely to miss action moving forward, so Hurst and the rest of Tampa Bay's offense may have a tough time getting into a rhythm with backup quarterback Jalon Daniels likely at the helm in Week 4 against the Packers.

items.headline: Myers made his only field-goal attempt, a 57 yarder, and all four of his extra-point tries in Sunday's 33-31 loss to the Commanders.
items.body: The veteran kicker remains perfect on the season, having now connected on all four field-goal tries and all nine extra-point attempts. The Seahawks are not doing much settling, but they are scoring, so Myers is getting enough chances to remain a strong fantasy play.

items.headline: Aubrey went three of four on field-goal tries and 2-for-2 on extra-point attempts in Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Ravens.
items.body: The kicker had a 59-yard attempt blocked in the third quarter. Aubrey has now missed one field goal and one extra point this season, though he is getting plenty of opportunities in Dallas' high-scoring offense, with nine extra-point attempts and seven field-goal tries through three games.

items.headline: Harris caught six of seven targets for 76 yards during Sunday's 24-16 loss to Buffalo.
items.body: Harris led the team in targets, receptions and receiving yards in the loss, all of which represented new career highs for the second-year pro. The wide receiver has now reeled in 10 of 16 targets for 149 yards over three games to open the regular season, and he appears to be on track to be a pivotal member of the team's passing attack in 2026.

items.headline: White rushed eight times for 35 yards and caught his only target for a six-yard touchdown during Sunday's 33-31 win over Seattle.
items.body: White was far more productive over his eight carries (4.4 YPC) than starting running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt was on his 19 rushes for 36 yards (1.9 YPC). However, White's most notable moment of the game came as a pass-catcher, as he secured a six-yard touchdown on a pass from Marcus Mariota in the first quarter. Through three games so far in the regular season, White has compiled 100 rushing yards on 22 carries while catching all nine of his targets for 51 yards and a score.

items.headline: Gesicki caught all three of his targets for 37 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 30-27 loss to Pittsburgh.
items.body: Gesicki took a step in the right direction after he was blanked in the team's Week 2 victory over Houston. The tight end was able to finished tied with wide receiver Dohnte Meyers for third on the team in catches, and he left his mark on the game in the fourth quarter, connecting with quarterback Joe Burrow for a 25-yard touchdown. Gesicki has now caught eight of 10 targets for 112 yards and two touchdowns over three regular-season contests so far in 2026.

items.headline: Gay made all three of his field-goal attempts and both extra-point tries in Sunday's 35-27 win over the Saints.
items.body: The kicker hit field goals from 41, 37 and 25 yards out, respectively, helping the Raiders light up the scoreboard. Gay has yet to miss this season, and the 3-0 Raiders have scored at least 26 points in every game.

items.headline: Mitchell rushed eight times for 52 yards and caught all three of his targets for minus-5 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 24-16 loss to the Bills.
items.body: Mitchell found himself far move involved on offense in Week 3, nearly matching his previous season total of nine carries while the three targets matched a career high. The running back reached paydirt in the first quarter, reeling in a one-yard pass from quarterback Justin Herbert. Mitchell remained the team's second option out of the backfield behind starter Omarion Hampton, but he proved that he could have standalone fantasy value if he gets more consistent touches moving forward.

items.headline: Harvey has been cleared to return to Sunday's game against the Rams after passing a concussion evaluation, Chris Tomasson of the Denver Gazette reports.
items.body: Harvey was evaluated for a concussion in the third quarter but has been cleared to return to action. He rejoins a Denver backfield that also includes J.K. Dobbins and Tyler Badie in the second half of Sunday night's game against the Rams.

items.headline: Ryland hit all three field-goal attempts and all three extra-point tries in Sunday's 36-30 loss to the 49ers.
items.body: The kicker's longest field goal came from 49 yards out. Ryland has only missed one kick this year, a 54-yard field-goal try. The Cardinals have also shown some life on offense, so if they continue to move the ball, Ryland will remain a fantasy-relevant option.

items.headline: Kupp caught four of five targets for 46 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 33-31 loss to the Commanders.
items.body: Kupp was able to take advantage of the return of quarterback Sam Darnold in Week 3, connecting with Darnold for a seven-yard score with 2:55 left in the fourth quarter. The wide receiver doubled his season total in targets Sunday, and he has now caught eight of 10 targets for 101 yards and a touchdown over three games so far in his second season with Seattle.

items.headline: Wilson caught three of six targets for 60 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 30-27 win over the Bengals.
items.body: Wilson came out of the gates hot Sunday, securing a 38-yard touchdown from quarterback Aaron Rodgers on the team's opening drive of the game. The wide receiver led the team in targets in Week 3, and he has now registered exactly six targets in each of the team's first three contests this season. Wilson has reeled in 11 of 18 targets for 114 yards and a touchdown so far this year.

items.headline: Harvey is being evaluated for a concussion, Parker Gabriel of the Denver Post reports.
items.body: Harvey was taken to the blue injury tent, and eventually to the locker room, to be evaluated for a concussion in the third quarter of Sunday's game against the Rams. The 2025 second-round pick will need to pass the evaluation to return to the game. J.K. Dobbins and Tyler Badie are Denver's available running backs. Harvey had two carries for six yards and caught five of six targets for 39 yards prior to coming off the field.

items.headline: Reichard hit all three field-goal attempts and both extra-point tries in Sunday's 23-16 win over the Bucs.
items.body: The kicker made field goals from 56, 54 and 43 yards, respectively. Reichard has yet to miss in 2026, and he has now connected on four field-goal tries from 50 yards or longer.

items.headline: Samuel turned two carries into 14 yards and scored an 80-yard touchdown during Sunday's 36-30 win over Arizona.
items.body: Samuel started off his day with a bang, receiving a lateral from fellow wideout Mike Evans during a hook-and-ladder play by San Francisco in the first quarter, taking off down the sideline for an 80-yard score. Samuel failed to catch a pass and didn't garner a target for the first time in three games this year, but he still found a way to make the most of limited opportunities. Evans suffered a rib/oblique injury in the second quarter of the victory, and if he's sidelined moving forward, Samuel will stand to operate as the team's No. 1 option at wide receiver.

items.headline: Prescott completed 25 of 40 passes for 276 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Ravens. He added 19 rushing yards on four carries and also threw a two-point conversion to CeeDee Lamb.
items.body: Despite the big numbers for the Cowboys on the scoreboard, Prescott had a relatively quiet day in Rio, with Jake Ferguson hauling in his only TD pass in the third quarter. Prescott didn't commit any turnovers for a second straight game, and through three weeks he's completed 69.5 percent of his passes (73-for-105) for 730 yards and a 7:1 TD:INT. The veteran QB will look to stay efficient in a Week 4 road trip to Houston.

items.headline: Meyers caught seven of eight targets for 64 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 35-6 win over New England.
items.body: Meyers led the team in targets, most notably reeling in a 10-yard score from quarterback Trevor Lawrence in the second quarter. The touchdown was the second of the year for the wide receiver, and he has now caught 10 of 11 targets for 132 yards over three contests in 2026. Parker Washington has established himself as Lawrence's favorite target, but Meyers has found himself on equal footing with fellow wideout Brian Thomas as an unpredictable fantasy asset early in the season.

items.headline: Pickens caught seven of 11 targets for 82 yards in Sunday's 34-31 loss to Baltimore.
items.body: The fifth-year wideout led the Cowboys in targets while setting new season highs in targets, catches and receiving yards, as he begins to shake off a slow start to the campaign. Pickens is still searching for his first TD of 2026, or even his first gain of 20-plus yards, but he'll look to continue building momentum in a Week 4 road trip to Houston.

items.headline: Brissett completed 38 of 52 passes for 280 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions and rushed four times for four yards in the Cardinals' 36-30 loss to the 49ers on Sunday.
items.body: Brissett put together one of his signature stat lines, parlaying massive passing volume into a solid yardage figure while remaining free of turnovers. The veteran signal-caller's pass-distribution profile also was on brand, as a whopping 28 of his pass attempts went in the direction of Michael Wilson (17 targets) and Trey McBride (11 targets). Brissett hit Wilson (five yards) and Jeremiyah Love (one yard) for his pair of touchdown passes, marking his first multi-TD tally of the season. Brissett is averaging a typically conservative 5.6 yards per attempt over his first three games, but he's thrown for over 275 yards twice to date heading into a Week 4 road matchup against the Giants next…

items.headline: Lamb caught seven of eight targets for 112 yards in Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Ravens. He also caught a two-point conversion.
items.body: George Pickens led the Cowboys in targets with 11, but it was Lamb who paced the team in receiving yards while the two star wideouts each tied for the team lead in receptions. This was the first game in 2026 during which Lamb failed to score a TD, but he has produced back-to-back performances of over 100 yards. He'll take a 20-309-3 line on 25 targets into a Week 4 road trip to Houston.

items.headline: Williams carried the ball 19 times for 98 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Ravens. He also caught two of three targets for five yards.
items.body: The veteran back gave the Cowboys a 10-0 lead in the first quarter with a two-yard TD plunge, his third trip to the end zone in three games this season, and Williams topped 100 scrimmage yards for the first time since Week 12 of 2025. Even with Sunday's strong effort, Williams has managed just 3,9 yards per carry to begin the year, a major downturn from his 4.8 mark in 2025. He'll look to keep building momentum in a Week 4 road trip to Houston.

items.headline: Harrison brought in three of five targets for 40 yards in the Cardinals' 36-30 loss to the 49ers on Sunday.
items.body: Harrison was a distant third in receiving yards and tied for the same slotting in targets for the Cardinals on the afternoon. Despite the modest stat line across the board, Harrison's Sunday was certainly an improvement on his Week 2, when he was blanked and saw only one target. While his season-high reception, receiving yardage and target totals offer some solace, they fall short of satisfying frustrated fantasy managers who banked on a comeback campaign from the 2024 first-round pick. Harrison still appears to clearly be behind Michael Wilson and Trey McBride in the Cardinals' pass-catching hierarchy heading into a Week 4 road matchup against the Giants next Sunday.

items.headline: Kittle brought in six of seven targets for 82 yards and two touchdowns in the 49ers' 36-30 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
